bull.b: The 108-qubit Cepheus system combines meaningful scale with strong reported fidelity and speed metrics, supporting Rigetti’s differentiation in superconducting quantum computing. This technical position may improve credibility with enterprise and government customers and support future system adoption.

Rapid year-over-year revenue growth and a substantial gross-margin improvement indicate early commercial traction and better economics on the current product mix. If on-premise systems and related orders continue scaling, these trends could gradually improve operating leverage over the next several quarters.

The definitive CHIPS Act agreement provides substantial nontraditional funding for cryogenic capacity, readout electronics and advanced fabrication. That support can accelerate processor development and infrastructure expansion while extending resources available for strategic quantum milestones, despite associated conditions.

bear.b: Rigetti remains far from self-funding, with substantial operating and free-cash-flow deficits requiring continued use of its capital base. Persistent burn could limit flexibility, increase dependence on external financing, and make execution of ambitious hardware investments more sensitive to cost overruns or delays.

Revenue growth is encouraging, but the absolute business scale remains small relative to Rigetti’s cost structure and investment needs. Dependence on system deliveries and government milestones can make results uneven, delaying the operating leverage and recurring revenue needed to support durable profitability.

The funding materially supports development but is not unconditional: later tranches depend on technical performance, and noncompliance may trigger clawbacks. These requirements add execution and reporting burdens, while government rights and issued shares may constrain flexibility and create dilution.
